What is Buy-side M&A? In one line: advice for a company or investor buying a business or asset.

It matters because a buyer can overpay or inherit hidden problems. Structured origination and diligence reduce that risk.

- Target search: identify businesses that fit the buyer's strategy, not just the obvious names.
- Valuation and structure: assess what the business is worth and how the purchase will be funded.
- Due diligence and negotiation: coordinate due diligence, negotiate and work towards completion.

Structured origination and diligence reduce the risk of overpaying or inheriting hidden problems.

Helping strategic acquirers, corporates and investors identify, assess and complete acquisitions is one of the things we do.

author: Nabih Eid
headline: PwC Germany | Deals · Carve-outs · Value Creation | Offering Lead, Carve-out Intelligence
text:
Buyers price uncertainty. In a carve-out, they price it twice.
 
Once in the valuation, and again in the share purchase agreement.
 
The uncertainty rarely sits in the business plan. It sits in what is still shared with the group: systems, people, contracts. Usually nobody has quantified it. So the buyer does.
 
That's the gap we set out to close with Carve-Out Intelligence.
 
Instead of weeks of workshops, we read the entanglement directly from the seller's own SAP data. The result is an IC-ready view of what is shared, how long separation takes, and what it costs, while the perimeter is still open.
 
The business doesn't change. What changes is who holds the facts.
 
In the recording of our PE webcast, Harry Schuster, Tobias Blaser and I walk through a complete assessment, from the first data extraction to the decision: → where the group and the business are still entangled → how long separation takes, and what it costs → how different perimeter options compare before going to market
 
Recording in the comments.
 
#PrivateEquity #CarveOut #MandA #ExitReadiness #PwC

text:
Private equity value creation is getting less glamorous and more measurable.

The winning playbook I see is not more initiatives. It is fewer initiatives with a tighter operating cadence.

A simple 3-layer model:
- Cash: working capital, capex discipline, and liquidity runway (weekly visibility).
- KPIs: one KPI tree per value driver, with owners and thresholds.
- Governance: decision rights, escalation rules, and a monthly exception process.

What to do next week:
Pick one value driver (pricing, churn, procurement, utilisation). Build the KPI tree on one slide. Agree the threshold that triggers action. Then stop tracking the vanity metrics.

Where do you see the biggest leakage: cash visibility, KPI ownership, or governance discipline?

#privateequity #valuecreation

author: Mohamed Bassuny, FMVA®, IFQ
headline: Middle East Banks @ Fitch Ratings | Credit Analysis, Islamic Banking
text:
Saudi banks' liquidity is likely to stay tight in 2027, and we see this as an increasingly structural shift rather than a temporary squeeze.

Credit demand linked to Vision 2030 continues to outpace growth in cheaper funding. In 3Q26, loans grew by about 2.4% while deposits contracted by about 1.8%. As a result, banks are relying more on term deposits and wholesale funding. Government-entity deposits at SAMA are near a five-year low, and the 3M SAIBOR–SOFR spread is about 130bp, well above the historical average of about 80bp.

We expect pressure on margins and credit growth of 8% in 2027. However, strong capitalisation and access to wholesale markets should keep tighter liquidity from materially constraining banks' ability to finance the economy.

Returning backers Mohamed Farouk, Algebra Ventures and DisrupTech Ventures led the $3.5 million pre-Series A round in the Egypt-based embedded finance and white-label card provider, according to Wamda. headline: محامي | قانون الشركات، مساعدة قانونية، الاستشارات القانونية
text:
يسعدني الإعلان عن حصولي على شهادة إتمام دورة تقييم الشركات الناشئة (Startup Valuation)، المقدمة من مركز مصر لريادة الأعمال والابتكار، تحت إشراف الدكتور/ فادي إسماعيل.

وقد أتاحت لي هذه الدورة فرصة لتعميق معرفتي بالمفاهيم والأساليب المالية والاستثمارية المستخدمة في تقييم الشركات الناشئة، وفهم آليات تحديد القيمة السوقية للشركات في مراحل نموها المختلفة، والتعرف على أبرز نماذج التقييم، ومنها:

* طريقة التدفقات النقدية المخصومة (Discounted Cash Flow – DCF).
* طريقة بيركوس (Berkus Method).
* تقييم حجم السوق والإمكانات الاستثمارية.
* تحليل المخاطر والفرص الاستثمارية.
* فهم العوامل المؤثرة في القيمة التقديرية للشركات الناشئة.

وتأتي هذه الخطوة في إطار حرصي على تطوير خبراتي القانونية والمالية، وتعزيز معرفتي بمجالات تأسيس الشركات، وحوكمة الشركات الناشئة، والامتثال القانوني، والاستثمار.

أؤمن بأن المحامي المتخصص في مجال الشركات لا يقتصر دوره على تقديم الدعم القانوني فحسب، بل يمتد ليكون شريكًا في فهم الأعمال ودعم القرارات الاستثمارية وتحقيق الاستدامة والنمو.

text:
The best time to prepare your business for an exit is 2-3 years before you want to sell. ⏳
Most owners start when they’re tired or a buyer calls. By then, it’s too late to fix what matters. Here’s what I’d do instead:
1. Make the business run without you. Buyers pay for a business, not a job. If every key decision, client and supplier relationship goes through you, expect a lower price and more earn-out.
2. Clean up your financials. Get audited or reviewed accounts, separate personal expenses, and be able to explain every adjustment to EBITDA. Messy books kill deals in diligence.
3. Show recurring, predictable cash flow. In the GCC today, buyers are paying for visible cash conversion. Multiples have been resetting, with 6x-8x EBITDA the most common range, so quality of earnings matters more than a good story.
4. Reduce concentration risk. One customer worth 40% of revenue, or one key supplier, will be discounted. Diversify early.
5. Build a second layer of management. A strong team that stays after the sale is worth real money to a buyer.
6. Tidy up legal and compliance. Licences, contracts, ownership structure, IP and employment records should all be in order before you open a data room.
7. Know your number, and your walk-away. Get an independent valuation and decide what you actually want: a full exit, a partial sale, or a phased handover.
Preparation won’t guarantee a premium price, but it will make your deal faster, cleaner and far less likely to collapse in the final wee

What interests me isn't just the announcement. It's the pattern.

Look at how KONČAR approaches international growth:

🇺🇸 Sanmina: A different model, combining transformer engineering expertise with an American manufacturing platform.

🇸🇦 Al Suwaiket: A local partner bringing market knowledge, business relationships, and project development capabilities.

Three different approaches. One underlying strategy.

Build strong engineering capabilities at home. Partner internationally for the capabilities and market access you need to grow.

text:
The Houthi missile that hit the Public Investment Fund's tower in Riyadh is being celebrated online as a blow to Saudi wealth, but what it damaged was an office block. Windows shattered across seven or eight floors of the tower in the King Abdullah Financial District on 19 November, which Saudi authorities blame on debris from an intercepted missile.

The fund makes nothing. It holds shares in banks, telecoms, miners and foreign companies, plus land for the giga projects, about SAR 2.16 trillion in securities on its 2025 accounts. None of that sits in the tower, and broken glass does not move a single share. The Aramco building hit in the same district on 8 November was the same, an office far from any well or terminal.

The cost falls on the image. The district was built to show foreign banks and funds a safe Riyadh, and two hits there in 11 days is what their risk desks will price.
